canonical_claim: The ASan battery scripts `build/asan_battery.sh` and `build/asan_battery2.sh` misidentified aborting tests because plain `grep` treated round logs containing embedded NUL bytes from CAS payloads as binary files. Additionally, The ASan battery's culprit-detection scripts used plain `grep` (not `grep -a`) on archived round logs containing thousands of embedded NUL bytes from CAS blob payloads in stdout, causing silent misattribution: rounds 27-66 (39 consecutive rounds) were all the same unfixed `CasRefSnapshotFormat.RejectsSnapshotIdBelowSealedFrom` abort, never actually excluded, so the peeling loop looped on one bug while accumulating ~30 wrong bystander test names in the known-debt list; the fix switched the scripts to `grep -a` and the exclusion list was corrected from 58 down to 28 verified real culprits. Additionally, Because of the binary-log parsing bug, `CasRefSnapshotFormat.RejectsSnapshotIdBelowSealedFrom` aborted rounds 27 through 66, a 39-round loop in which the battery accumulated false bystander exclusions instead of converging. Additionally, The ASan culprit detector must use `grep -a` for round logs, and the corrected `build/asan_battery_aborted.txt` contains 28 verified real culprits rather than the previous 58-name list; the bogus list is preserved as `build/asan_battery_aborted.txt.bak_bogus`.; Completed unfiltered `unit_tests_dbms` logs can contain NUL bytes and omit the beginning of redirected stdout; use `grep -a`, keep completion markers in a separate small file, and rely on the surviving gtest summary for totals.
